method: ENTIRELY from AMH, read under subscription and PARAPHRASED: no passage reproduced, no source_text stored, every claim carries the locator for the page it came from and the verdict licensed_source_not_quoted, so NOTHING here is machine re-checkable. A targeted search found no open current Australian source for this topic; that absence is recorded rather than papered over with an older article. Onset and duration figures from the two comparison tables are flagged dose:true because they are what determines the choice of agent and how long the patient is impaired.

claims.claim: Topical anticholinergics aid eye examination by causing mydriasis, meaning pupil dilation, and cycloplegia, meaning paralysis of accommodation
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Mydriasis and cycloplegia' (Eye drugs > Drugs for eye examinations and procedures) at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/eye-drugs/drugs-eye-examinations/mydriasis-cycloplegia, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22
